- Record ID: 410e4766ea4b9e01
  - Candidate: F-02
  - Fact-card IDs: []
  - Provenance: {"char_end":1567,"char_start":1102,"file":"inputs/trials/formulation-trial-02.docx","page":2}
  - Quote:
<!-- qbd-verbatim-quote:start -->
Observations
 Direct compression showed poorer flow than wet granulation (Carr index 24%).
 Dissolution is slower than F-01 but still meets specification.
 Hardness range is wider - compression force control is more critical.
 Higher disintegrant level (5%) compensates for lack of granule bonding.
 Content uniformity AV is higher (11.2 vs 6.8), indicating mixing is less homogeneous.
     Simplified process (fewer steps) reduces manufacturing time by ~40%.
<!-- qbd-verbatim-quote:end -->

- Record ID: bb3d0ec5ce9962d9
  - Candidate: F-03
  - Fact-card IDs: []
  - Provenance: {"char_end":1817,"char_start":1381,"file":"inputs/trials/formulation-trial-03.docx","page":2}
  - Quote:
<!-- qbd-verbatim-quote:start -->
Observations
 Higher dose (10 mg) gives better content uniformity (AV 5.4) due to lower relative potency
    variation.
 Dissolution is fastest among all three formulations - higher drug load creates more porous
    granules.
 Hardness is highest (72 N) - good mechanical stability.
 Binder level increased (8 mg vs 5 mg) to accommodate higher drug loading.
 Yellow coating distinguishes 10 mg from 5 mg (white) for patient safety.
<!-- qbd-verbatim-quote:end -->
